title: Equity finance
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:33Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest point, bus-financing-new-business, contrasts the owner's own money with borrowed debt for a new business, while this point covers raising money by selling shares through the ASX or private equity, which is a different and more specific Year 12 idea.

draft.title: Equity finance
card: Equity finance is money a business raises by selling part of its ownership. The buyers become owners, called shareholders.

a company can sell these to the public on the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX) once it is listed. Ordinary shareholders may receive dividends, which are a share of profit, and usually get voting rights.
a private equity investor buys a share of a business that is not listed on the ASX. The investor often brings advice as well as money.
The business has no loan to repay and pays no interest on this money. In return, ownership is shared, so the original owners have less say and a smaller share of the profits.
draft.remember: Equity finance raises money by selling ownership, so there is nothing to repay but control is shared.

a.q: Which feature is typical of raising money through equity finance?
opts: There is no loan to repay, but ownership is shared
The money must be repaid in fixed instalments
The lender takes a claim over a business asset
The owners keep full control of the business
a.why: Equity buyers become part owners, so the business owes them no repayment of the money. The cost is shared ownership. Full control is tempting, but selling shares gives others a say.
a.clue: Think about what the buyers of shares receive in return for their money.

b.q: Priya owns all of Kora Pty Ltd, a fast-growing bakery chain in Perth. She sells 30% of the business to a private equity investor for $2 million. What is the main drawback for Priya?
opts: She now shares ownership and a share of future profits
She must repay the $2 million with interest each month
She must list Kora on the ASX and publish its accounts
She has to hand over a business asset as security
b.why: Selling 30% makes the investor a part owner, so Priya has less control and 30% of future profit goes to the investor. Repayments with interest are tempting, but equity money is not a loan and carries no interest.
b.clue: The investor bought part of the business, not lent money to it.

a.best: There is no loan to repay, but ownership is shared

b.best: She now shares ownership and a share of future profits
